Whether it be incense powder, incense balls, or ointments, those who uphold this sutra will be able to distinguish them all while remaining right here.

Furthermore, they will specifically know the scents of sentient beings—the scents of elephants, horses, oxen, sheep, and so forth; the scents of men, women, boys, and girls; as well as the scents of grasses, trees, and forests. Whether near or far, they shall hear and distinguish all such scents without error.

Those who uphold this sutra, though dwelling here on earth, shall likewise perceive the fragrances of the various devas in the heavens: the scents of the pārijātaka and kovidāra trees; the fragrance of māndārava flowers, mahāmāndārava flowers, mañjūṣaka flowers, and mahāmañjūṣaka flowers; and the various powdered incenses of sandalwood and aloeswood, as well as the scents of diverse blossoms. Of all such celestial perfumes, produced from the blending of these elements, there is none they do not perceive or know.

Furthermore, they smell the fragrances of the bodies of the various devas: the fragrance when Śakra-devānām-indra is upon his magnificent palace, enjoying and sporting in the pleasures of the five senses;
the fragrance when he is in the Hall of the Sublime Dharma, preaching the Dharma for the Trāyastriṃśa devas;
the fragrance when he sports in the various gardens; and the fragrances of the bodies of the men and women of the other devas—all of these they smell from afar.
In this manner, proceeding by successive stages up to the Brahma Heaven and reaching as far as the Peak of Existence (Bhavāgra), they likewise smell the bodily fragrances of all the devas;

furthermore, they smell the incense burned by the devas, as well as the fragrances of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and the bodily fragrances of all Buddhas, perceiving them all from afar and knowing their locations.
"Although they smell these fragrances, their faculty of the nose is neither impaired nor deluded; if they wish to discern them and explain them to others, their recollection is unerring.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"The nose of this person is pure; within this world,"
Whether fragrant or foul, all various things are smelled and known.
The scents of sumana and jāti, tamāla and sandalwood, agallochum and cinnamon,
and the fragrances of various flowers and fruits— [all are perceived].
He also knows the scents of sentient beings— the scents of men and women—
and though the teacher of the Dharma dwells afar, he perceives their location by their scent.
He likewise knows the great powerful wheel-turning kings, the minor wheel-turners, and their sons.
The ministers and the palace ladies, by smelling the fragrance, know where they are;
the precious jewels worn upon their bodies, as well as the treasures hidden within the earth,
and the precious women of the Wheel-Turning King— all these are known by their location through the scent.
The various ornaments with which people adorn their bodies—
clothing, necklaces, and the diverse scents they apply— their persons are known by the scent alone.
Whether the devas are walking or sitting, whether they are sporting or manifesting supernatural transformations, [all is known].
Those who uphold this Lotus Sutra can perceive everything by its fragrance:
the flowers, fruits, and seeds of all trees, as well as the scents of ghee and oil;
while abiding here, those who uphold the sutra know the location of them all.
In the deep and perilous places among the mountains, where sandalwood trees are in full bloom,
those sentient beings dwelling therein can all perceive them by their fragrance.
Within the Cakravāḍa mountains and the great oceans, as well as among all sentient beings upon the earth—
Those who uphold this sutra will, by smelling fragrances, know the locations of all beings:
the male and female asuras, along with their various retinues;
when they are engaged in strife or play, those who uphold the sutra can know it all by smelling their fragrance.
In vast wildernesses and perilous defiles, lions, elephants, tigers, wolves, wild oxen,
water buffaloes, and the like, their locations are known by the scent;
likewise, if there is one who is pregnant, whether it be male or female is discerned before birth.
Rootless beings and non-humans— by smelling their fragrance, he knows them all.
By the power of smelling fragrance, he knows when one has first conceived,
whether the pregnancy will be successful or not, and whether she will give birth in peace to a blessed child.
By the power of smelling fragrances, one knows the thoughts of men and women—their minds of lust, delusion, and anger—as well as those who cultivate virtue.
One also knows the various hidden treasures beneath the earth: gold, silver, and all manner of precious gems.
Whatever is contained within bronze vessels, he can know by smelling its fragrance.
Regarding various kinds of necklaces and ornaments, none can recognize their value;
yet by smelling the fragrance, he knows their worth—whether they are precious or common—and their origin and current location.
The various celestial flowers, such as the māndārava, mañjūṣaka, and pārijātaka trees—
by smelling their fragrance, one can know them all. One also knows the celestial palaces,
with their distinctions of superior, middling, and inferior.
Adorned with various precious flowers, they can know them all by smelling their fragrance.
In celestial gardens, groves, and sublime palaces, within the various pavilions and halls of wondrous Dharma, they enjoy themselves; by smelling their fragrance, they can know them all.
Whether the devas are listening to the Dharma, or enjoying the five desires, or moving about,
walking, sitting, or reclining— their coming and going— he perceives them all by their fragrance.
He also knows the garments worn by the celestial maidens, adorned with exquisite flowers and perfumes.
While moving about and sporting, they can perceive all scents;
thus proceeding upward in succession, even unto the Brahma Heaven,
those who enter and emerge from meditative absorption can perceive all scents by means of their fragrance.
From the Ābhāsvara and Śubhakṛtsna heavens up to the Peak of Existence (Bhavāgra),
he can perceive through the scent of their birth and their passing away;
likewise, he knows all the assemblies of bhikṣus who are ever diligent in the Dharma.
Whether sitting or walking, or reciting the sutras and Dharma,
or staying beneath forest trees, or sitting in meditative concentration with single-minded devotion—
the upholder of the sutras, by smelling their fragrance, knows exactly where they are.
The Bodhisattva’s resolve is firm and steadfast; whether sitting in meditation, reading the sutras, or preaching the Dharma to others, he can perceive everything by its fragrance.
Wherever the World-Honored Ones may be, who are revered by all, [he knows them all].
Out of compassion for the multitude, he preaches the Dharma; by smelling their fragrance, he knows them all.
Sentient beings standing before the Buddha, hearing the sutras, all rejoice;
practicing according to the Dharma, by smelling their fragrance, he knows them all.
"Although they have not yet attained the bodhisattva state, the untainted dharma arises in their nose;
yet this upholder of the sutra first attains these characteristics of the nose.
Furthermore, Constantly Diligent One!"

If a son or daughter of good family receives, upholds, reads, recites, explains, or transcribes this sutra, they shall obtain twelve hundred merits of the tongue. Whether it be something pleasant or unpleasant, delicious or not delicious, or even bitter and astringent things, once they come into contact with their tongue-root, they will all transform into a supreme flavor, like celestial ambrosia, such that there is nothing that is not delicious.

If, by means of the faculty of the tongue, one delivers a discourse within the great assembly, emitting a profound and wondrous voice that can penetrate their hearts, causing them all to feel joy and happiness.

Furthermore, the sons of gods, daughters of gods, Śakra, Brahmā, and all the other devas, having heard this profound and wondrous sound and the orderly sequence of the discourse being expounded, all came to listen.

Furthermore, nāgas and nāga maidens, yakṣas and yakṣī maidens, gandharvas and gandharvī maidens, asuras and asurī maidens, garuḍas and garuḍī maidens, kiṃnaras and kiṃnarī maidens, mahoragas and mahoragī maidens all came to attend upon him out of a desire to hear the Dharma, approaching him with reverence and making offerings.

Also present were bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās; kings, princes, ministers, and their retinues; and minor and great wheel-turning monarchs (cakravartins) with their seven treasures and thousand sons, along with their inner and outer entourages, all arriving together in their celestial palaces to listen to the Dharma.
Because this bodhisattva skillfully expounds the Dharma, brahmins, householders, and all the people within the kingdom serve and make offerings to him for as long as they live.

Furthermore, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and buddhas always delight in seeing him. In whichever direction this person resides, all buddhas turn toward that place to preach the Dharma for him. He is able to receive and uphold all the Buddha-dharmas, and can also produce profound and wondrous sounds of the Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"The tongue-faculty of this person is pure, And they shall never experience unpleasant flavors;
Whatever they consume and eat Shall all become nectar."
With a voice that is profound, pure, and wondrous, he preaches the Dharma to the great assembly;
through various causes, conditions, and parables, he guides the minds of sentient beings.
All who hear it rejoice and present the most excellent offerings.
The devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and asuras alike,
with hearts full of reverence, all come together to listen to the Dharma.
If this person who preaches the Dharma wishes to use a wondrous voice,
Pervading the trichiliocosm, he can reach any place at will.
The great and small wheel-turning kings, along with their retinues of a thousand sons,
join their palms with a heart of reverence and constantly come to listen to and receive the Dharma.
The devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and piśācas,
with hearts full of joy, also constantly delight in coming to make offerings.
Brahmā, the King of Māras, Īśvara, and Maheśvara—
Thus, the hosts of devas constantly come to his abode;
the Buddhas and their disciples, hearing the sound of his preaching the Dharma,
always keep him in mind and protect him, sometimes manifesting themselves before him.
"Furthermore, Constantly Diligent!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, upholds, reads, recites, explains, or transcribes this sutra, they shall obtain eight hundred merits of the body and attain a pure body like clear lapis lazuli.

Because sentient beings delight in seeing the purity of their body, the beings of the trichiliocosm—at birth, at death, ascending or descending, handsome or ugly, born in good or evil realms—all appear within it. Furthermore, the Iron Ring Mountains, the Great Iron Ring Mountains, Mount Meru, Mount Mahāmeru, and all other mountains, as well as the sentient beings therein, all appear within it."
From the Avīci Hell below up to the Peak of Existence above, all things and all sentient beings appear within it.
Whether it be Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, or Buddhas preaching the Dharma, the forms and images of them all appear within his body.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"If one upholds the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, Their body shall be exceedingly pure,
Like that of clear lapis lazuli, Such that all sentient beings rejoice at the sight."
Just as a pure, bright mirror reflects all forms and images, so too does the Bodhisattva, within his pure body, perceive everything that exists in the world.
He alone perceives with perfect clarity; what others cannot see, he sees.
Within the three thousandfold world system, all living beings—
gods, humans, asuras, those in the hells, hungry ghosts, and animals—
all such forms and appearances manifest within his body.
The palaces of the various devas, up to the Summit of Existence (bhavāgra),
the Iron Ring Mountains (cakravāḍa) and Mount Meru,
as well as Mount Mahāmeru and all the waters of the great oceans— all these appear within his body.
The Buddhas and their śrāvakas, as well as the Bodhisattvas, the children of the Buddha—
whether alone or in the assembly— they all manifest when preaching the Dharma.
Although they have not yet attained the stainless, wondrous body of the dharma-nature, [they manifest it].
"By means of the pure, eternal essence, everything manifests within it.
Furthermore, Constantly Diligent!

If good men or good women, after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, or transcribe this sutra, they shall attain twelve hundred merits of the mental faculty. By means of this purified mental faculty, even upon hearing a single verse or a single phrase, they will penetrate immeasurable and boundless meanings."

Having understood this meaning, one is able to expound upon a single phrase or a single verse for a month, four months, or even a year; all the teachings thus proclaimed, according to their underlying significance, shall never contradict the true nature of reality (bhūtalakṣaṇa).

If he speaks of worldly scriptures, secular discourse, or the various means of livelihood, all of these accord with the True Dharma; furthermore, he fully knows the mental activities, mental movements, and mental conceptual proliferations of all sentient beings throughout the six realms within the trichiliocosm.

Although they have not yet attained untainted wisdom (*anāsrava-jñāna*), their mental faculty (*manas-indriya*) is thus purified; whatever they contemplate, deliberate upon, or express in speech is entirely the Buddha-dharma and nothing but truth, and it is also that which was taught in the sūtras of the Buddhas of the past.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to reiterate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"The mind of this person is pure, Luminous, sharp, and free from defilement.
By means of this wondrous faculty of mind, They know the dharmas of superior, middling, and inferior."
Even upon hearing a single verse, they penetrate immeasurable meanings;
they explain them in sequence according to the Dharma, for months, four months, or even a year.
To all sentient beings, both within and without this world, [they teach].
Whether they be devas, nāgas, or humans, yakṣas, or spirits,
those who dwell within the six realms of existence— the various kinds of thoughts they harbor—
are all known at once through the retribution of upholding the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.
The countless Buddhas of the ten directions, Whose marks are adorned with a hundred merits, preach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings;
I hear them all and am able to receive and uphold it, contemplating their immeasurable meanings; Their preaching of the Dharma is likewise immeasurable.
From beginning to end they never forget their practice, because they uphold the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.
They fully know the characteristics of all phenomena, recognize their sequence according to their meaning, and master names and language; they preach exactly as they have understood.
Whatever this person speaks is entirely the Dharma of the former Buddhas;
because they expound this Dharma, they are without fear among the multitude.
One who upholds the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* has a faculty of mind as pure as this.
Although they have not yet attained the outflows-free state, they already possess such signs.
This person who upholds this sutra dwells in a rare and sublime stage;
for the sake of all sentient beings, they are joyful, beloved, and honored.
Able to expound the Dharma through thousands of millions of kinds of skillful speech,
it is because they uphold the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
Chapter Nineteen: The Bodhisattva Never Disparaging. At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta:
"You should now know this!"

If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who uphold the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* should encounter those who speak with harsh words, revile them, or slander them, they will receive a retribution for their great sin as previously described;
yet the merit they shall obtain will be as previously stated: their eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind will become pure.
Mahāsthāmaprāpta!

In the distant past, beyond immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there was a Buddha named King of Majestic Sound (*Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja*), a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān. The kalpa was named Free from Decline (*Vigatavyaya*), and the land was named Great Achievement (*Mahāsiddhi*).

That Buddha King of Majestic Sound, within that world, preached the Dharma for devas, humans, and asuras; for those seeking the vehicle of the śrāvaka, he taught the Dharma corresponding to the Four Noble Truths, leading them across birth, old age, sickness, and death to ultimate nirvāṇa.
For those seeking the state of a pratyekabuddha, he teaches the Dharma corresponding to the twelve links of dependent origination.
For all bodhisattvas, for the sake of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, he teaches the Dharma corresponding to the six pāramitās, culminating in the wisdom of a Buddha.
Mahāsthāmaprāpta!

The lifespan of that Buddha King of Majestic Sound was forty trillion nayutas of Ganges-sands of kalpas; the duration of his True Dharma remaining in the world was equal to the number of kalpas represented by the dust motes of one Jambudvīpa;
and the duration of his Semblance Dharma remaining in the world was equal to the number of kalpas represented by the dust motes of the four continents.
After that Buddha had extensively benefited sentient beings, he then entered parinirvāṇa.

Following the complete extinction of both the True Dharma and the Semblance Dharma, another Buddha appeared in this land, likewise named Vairocana-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān; in this manner, there were twenty trillion Buddhas in succession, all bearing the same name.

After the Tathāgata King of Majestic Sound had first entered parinirvāṇa, and following the extinction of the True Dharma, during the period of the Semblance Dharma, monks of overweening pride possessed great power.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva bhikṣu named Sadāparibhūta.
Mahāsthāmaprāpta!
For what reason was he named Sadāparibhūta?
Whatever bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās this bhikṣu sees, he bows to and praises them all, saying:
"I deeply respect you all; I do not dare to treat you with contempt."
"Why is this? Because you all practice the bodhisattva path and shall attain Buddhahood.
Yet this bhikṣu did not devote himself exclusively to reading and reciting the sūtras, but practiced only prostrations.
Even when he saw the fourfold assembly from afar, he would still go to them to pay homage and offer praise, saying:
"I do not dare to treat you with contempt; you shall all become Buddhas."
Among the fourfold assembly, there were those who gave rise to thoughts of anger and impurity, speaking with harsh words and insults, saying: "From where has this ignorant bhikṣu come?
He says of himself: 'I do not slight you; I bestow upon you the prediction that you shall become buddhas.'"
"We have no need for such false predictions.
Thus, though he was constantly reviled for many years, he did not give rise to anger, but always spoke these words:
"You shall become a Buddha."
When these words were spoken, the crowd struck and pelted him with sticks, wood, tiles, and stones.
He fled to a distant place to stay, yet continued to cry out in a loud voice:
"I dare not slight you; you shall all become Buddhas."
Because he constantly spoke these words, the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who were possessed of overweening pride (adhimāna) called him "Never-Disparaging" (Sadāparibhūta).

"When this bhikṣu was approaching the end of his life, he heard in the midst of space the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* previously preached by the Buddha King of Majestic Voice, consisting of twenty koṭis of nayutas of verses; he was able to receive and uphold them all. He immediately attained the aforementioned purity of the faculty of the eye, as well as the purity of the faculties of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Having attained this purity of the six faculties, his lifespan increased by two hundred koṭis of nayutas of years, and he extensively expounded this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* for others."

At that time, the fourfold assembly of those with overweening pride—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—who had looked down upon this person and given him the name "Not-Disdainful," saw that he had attained the power of great supernormal faculties, the power of eloquence in joyful exposition, and the power of great sublime tranquility; hearing what he taught, they all believed, submitted, and followed him.

This Bodhisattva further transformed and converted thousands of myriads of koṭis of beings, causing them to dwell in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. After his life came to an end, he encountered two thousand koṭis of Buddhas, all named Candrasūryapradīpa (Moon-Sun-Lamp), who preached this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* within their respective teachings. By these causes and conditions, he further encountered two thousand koṭis of Buddhas, all of whom were likewise named Meghasvararāja (Cloud-Sovereign-Lamp-King).

Because they receive, uphold, read, and recite these teachings of the Buddhas, and expound this sūtra for the sake of the fourfold assembly, they attain this constant purity of the eye, as well as the purity of the faculties of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; thus, they preach the Dharma among the fourfold assembly with a mind free from fear.

“Mahāsthāmaprāpta! This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Constantly Non-Disparaging made offerings to as many Buddhas as these, honoring, respecting, and praising them, thereby planting various roots of goodness. Later, he further encountered thousands of myriads of koṭis of Buddhas, and likewise preached this sutra within the teachings of those Buddhas. Having accomplished such merit, he shall surely attain Buddhahood.”
Mahāsthāmaprāpta! What do you think?
Was the Bodhisattva Never Disparaging at that time anyone other than this person?
I am that very person.
Had I not, in past lives, upheld, recited, and read this sutra, and had I not explained it to others, I would not have been able to quickly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
because I upheld, recited, and read this sutra and explained it to others before the former Buddhas, I have quickly attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Mahāsthāmaprāpta!

Because those four assemblies of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās at that time treated me with contempt out of anger and malice, for two hundred billion kalpas they never encountered a Buddha, heard the Dharma, or saw the Saṃgha; for a thousand kalpas they underwent great suffering and affliction in the Avīci Hell.
Once these karmic retributions were exhausted, they again encountered the Bodhisattva Never-Disparaging, who taught and transformed them toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Mahāsthāmaprāpta! What do you think?
Were those members of the fourfold assembly who constantly disparaged this bodhisattva at that time anyone other than yourself?

In this assembly now, there are five hundred bodhisattvas such as Bhadrapāla, five hundred bhikṣus such as Siṃhacandra, and five hundred upāsakas such as Niścitabuddhi; all of them are non-retrogressive regarding anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Mahāsthāmaprāpta!

You should know that this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* brings great benefit to all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and is able to lead them to anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. For this reason, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should constantly receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, and transcribe this sūtra.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke these verses:
"In the past there was a Buddha, Named King of Majestic Sound;
His spiritual wisdom was immeasurable, And he led all beings— Gods, humans, dragons, and spirits— All of whom made offerings to him together."
After this Buddha has passed away, when the Dharma is about to perish, there will be a bodhisattva named Sadāparibhūta.
At that time, the fourfold assembly will be attached to their own views of the Dharma; the Bodhisattva Sadāparibhūta will go to them and say to them:
"I do not slight you; as you all practice the Way, you shall all become Buddhas.
When the people heard this, they treated him with contempt, reviled, and abused him;
yet the Bodhisattva Never-Disparaging was able to endure it all.
Having heard this sutra, their six sense faculties become pure;
by the power of their supernormal abilities, they increase their lifespan and further expound this sutra extensively for all people.
The multitude who were attached to various dharmas, all received the Bodhisattva’s teaching and transformation, achieving perfection and being established in the Buddha-way.
After Ajita’s life ended, he encountered countless Buddhas; because he preached this sutra, he obtained immeasurable merit.
Gradually perfecting his merit, he swiftly attained the Buddha-way.
At that time, "Not-Disparaging" was none other than my own self.
As for the fourfold assembly who were attached to the Dharma at that time, they heard the words of Not-Disparaging:
"You shall become a Buddha.
By these causes and conditions, they have encountered countless Buddhas.
These bodhisattvas in this assembly, the multitude of five hundred, as well as the fourfold assembly—
The laymen and laywomen of pure faith who are now here before me listening to the Dharma are these very people.
In previous lives, I exhorted all these individuals to listen to and receive this sutra,
the supreme teaching.
They reveal and teach others, causing them to dwell in nirvana; from lifetime to lifetime they uphold such a sutra as this.
Only after billions of billions of kalpas, reaching the inconceivable, do they finally hear this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
Throughout billions upon billions of kalpas, even unto the inconceivable, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
have at times preached this sutra;
therefore, practitioners, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, upon hearing such a sutra as this, must not give rise to doubt or confusion.
"You should with single-mindedness widely expound this sutra; you shall encounter Buddhas in every lifetime and swiftly attain the Buddha-way. Chapter 20:

The Supernatural Powers of the Tathāgata *The Added Chapter of the Lotus Sutra of the Marvelous Law, Chapter Twenty: The Supernatural Powers of the Tathāgata* At that time, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as numerous as the atoms in a thousand worlds, who had leaped forth from the earth, all stood before the Buddha with single-minded palms joined. Gazing up at the Honored Countenance, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"After the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha, wherever the emanations of the World-Honored One may pass into extinction in various lands, we shall extensively preach this sutra there. Why is this? "
"We ourselves also wish to obtain this true, pure, and great Dharma, to receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, transcribe, and make offerings to it.

At that time, the World-Honored One, before Mañjuśrī and the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had long resided in the Sahā world, as well as before all the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and the entire assembly, manifested great supernormal power. He extended his broad and long tongue until it reached the Brahma-world, and from every pore he emitted immeasurable and innumerable rays of light of various colors, which completely illuminated the worlds of the ten directions.
The Buddhas seated upon lion thrones beneath the various jewel trees were likewise so; they extended their broad and long tongues and emitted immeasurable light.

When Śākyamuni Buddha and the Buddhas beneath the jewel trees manifested this supernatural power, a full hundred thousand years passed. Thereafter, they withdrew their tongue-phenomena and simultaneously cleared their throats and snapped their fingers. These two sounds reached all the Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions, and the earth everywhere shook in six ways.

Among them, the sentient beings—gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth—by the Buddha’s spiritual power, all beheld the Buddhas beneath the countless, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of jewel-trees on lion thrones in this Sahā world;
they also saw Śākyamuni Buddha together with the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna seated upon a lion throne within the jeweled stupa;
and they further saw countless, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The fourfold assembly also surrounded Śākyamuni Buddha with reverence.
Having seen this, they were all filled with great joy at such an unprecedented occurrence.
Immediately, the devas in the midst of the void cried out in a loud voice:

“Beyond these immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of asaṃkhyeya worlds, there is a land named Sahā. Therein dwells a Buddha named Śākyamuni, who is now preaching for the sake of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas a Mahāyāna sūtra titled ‘The Lotus of the Wonderful Law, Teaching the Dharma for Bodhisattvas, Protected by the Buddhas. You all should rejoice with deep hearts and should also pay homage and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha.”
Having heard the voice from the midst of space, those sentient beings joined their palms toward the Sahā world and spoke these words:
"Namo Śākyamuni Buddha!"
"Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha!

With various flowers, incense, necklaces, banners, canopies, and all manner of ornaments for the body, as well as rare jewels and exquisite objects, they all together scattered them from afar toward the Sahā world. The various items scattered from the ten directions gathered like clouds and transformed into jeweled curtains, covering all the Buddhas within this realm.
At that time, the worlds of the ten directions were unimpeded and interconnected, as if they were a single buddha-field.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the great assembly of bodhisattvas, including Śūraṅgama and the others:

"The spiritual power of the Buddhas is thus: immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable. Even if I were to use such spiritual power to proclaim the merits of this sutra for the sake of entrustment throughout immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, I could not exhaust them.

To speak of it in brief: all dharmas possessed by the Tathāgata, all sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata, all secret and essential treasuries of the Tathāgata, and all most profound matters of the Tathāgata are proclaimed and fully revealed within this sutra."
Therefore, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, you should with a single mind receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, copy, and practice according to the teaching.

In whatever land this person may dwell, if they uphold, read, recite, explain, copy, or practice according to the teaching; or wherever the sutra scrolls may be located—whether in a garden, a grove, beneath a tree, in a monastery, in a layperson’s house, in a hall, or in a mountain valley or wilderness—in all such places one should erect a stupa and make offerings.

Why is this? You should know that this place is itself the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa); it is here that all Buddhas attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, it is here that all Buddhas turn the wheel of Dharma, and it is here that all Buddhas enter parinirvāṇa.
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke in verse: "The Buddhas, saviors of the world, Abiding in great supernormal powers,
For the sake of gladdening sentient beings, Manifest immeasurable spiritual transformations."
The mark of his tongue reaches the Brahma-heaven; from his body he emits countless rays of light.
For those who seek the Buddha-way, he manifests these rare and wondrous events.
The sound of the Buddhas’ coughing and clearing of their throats, as well as the sound of their snapping fingers—
The sounds were heard throughout the lands of the ten directions, and the earth shook in six ways.
Because they are able to uphold this sutra after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa,
all Buddhas rejoice and manifest immeasurable supernatural powers.
Because I entrust this sutra to you, even if one were to praise those who receive and uphold it for immeasurable eons,
one could still not exhaust the description of that person’s merit; it is boundless and inexhaustible.
Just as the empty space of the ten directions has no perceivable limit,
so too those who can uphold this sutra have already seen me,
as well as the Buddha Prabhūtaratna and all his emanations.
Furthermore, they see me today teaching and transforming all bodhisattvas;
those who are able to uphold this sutra cause me, my emanations,
and the Buddha Many Treasures who has entered parinirvāṇa, to all rejoice.
The Buddhas of the ten directions currently present, as well as those of the past and future—
I behold them all and make offerings to them, causing them all to attain joy.
The secret and essential Dharma attained by all Buddhas while seated at the site of enlightenment—
Those who are able to uphold this sutra will, before long, likewise attain it.
Those who are able to uphold this sutra will, regarding the meaning of all dharmas,
their names, and their verbal expressions, delight in explaining them without end.
Just as the wind moves through space without any obstruction, so too,

after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, one should explain the sūtras spoken by the Buddha according to their causes and conditions and their sequential order, expounding them truthfully in accordance with their meaning.
Just as the light of the sun and moon can dispel all darkness,
so this person, walking through the world, can extinguish the gloom of sentient beings;
they instruct immeasurable bodhisattvas, causing them ultimately to abide in the One Vehicle.
Therefore, those who possess wisdom, having heard these merits and benefits,
should uphold this sutra after my parinirvāṇa;
such persons will have no doubt whatsoever regarding the Buddha-way.

Chapter 21: Dhāraṇī. In the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, Chapter Twenty-one, the Dhāraṇī Chapter: At that time, the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If there are good sons or good daughters who are able to receive and uphold the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, or who read and recite it until they have mastered it, or who transcribe its scrolls—how much merit will they obtain?
The Buddha told Bhaiṣajyarāja:
"If there were good sons or good daughters who made offerings to as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in eight hundred million nayutas of Ganges Rivers, what do you think?"
"Would the merit obtained thereby be great?
"It would be very great, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

"If any good man or good woman is able, regarding this sutra, to even receive and uphold a single four-line verse, reciting it, explaining its meaning, and practicing according to the teaching, their merit will be exceedingly great."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I shall now bestow upon the one who preaches this Dharma a dhāraṇī mantra to protect them.”
He then spoke the mantra, saying: "Tadugadidye ta (1) aniruddhe (2)"

"I, too, shall use *dhāraṇī* mantras to protect those who uphold the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.

This dhāraṇī mantra has been spoken by forty-two billion Buddhas; if anyone should injure or destroy this Dharma-preacher, they would thereby have injured and destroyed these Buddhas.

At that time, there were rākṣasīs, namely: first, Lambā; second, Vilambā; third, Kuḍṛṣṭi; fourth, Puṣpadantī; fifth, Kālīdantī; sixth, Bahuruci; seventh, Atṛptā; eighth, Mālyadhārī; ninth, Kaustukī; and tenth, Sarvasattvaujoharā. These ten rākṣasīs, together with Hārītī and her sons and retinue, went to where the Buddha was and addressed him with one voice, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

I, too, desire to protect those who read, recite, receive, and uphold the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, removing their misfortunes and afflictions; and should there be anyone who seeks out the faults of the Dharma Master, I shall ensure they find no opportunity to do so.

"Tadyathā | ididugami (recite this one phrase five times) | nindugami (also recite five times) | huluhuhudi (also recite five times) | sādudughe (also recite five times)."
"Rather let it fall upon my head than cause affliction to the Dharma-preacher— whether it be a yakṣa,
a rākṣasa, a preta, a pūtana, a kiṭika, a vetāla, a kumbhāṇḍa, an umaruka, an āvadhmātaka, or a yakṣakiṭika."
Whether it be a person afflicted by *jivhika* (sore throat), or a feverish illness—whether lasting one day, two days, three days, four days, or even up to seven days; whether it be a chronic fever;
or whether it takes the form of a man, a woman, a boy, or a girl—even within a dream, let there be none [of these afflictions].
"to cause affliction. Then, before the Buddha, he spoke in verse:

His head shall split into seven pieces, like the fruit of the *māluka* tree;
The sin is equal to that of killing one's father and mother, And likewise the calamity of crushing sesame for oil;
The crime of deceiving others with false measures and scales, And the offense of Devadatta in causing a schism in the Saṃgha.
"Whoever offends against this Dharma Master shall incur such calamities as these.
After the rākṣasīs had spoken this verse, they addressed the Buddha, saying:

We, too, shall personally protect those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and practice this sutra, causing them to attain peace and security, to be free from all calamities and afflictions, and to neutralize all poisons.
The Buddha addressed the rākṣasīs: “Excellent, excellent!

If you can merely protect those who receive and uphold the name of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, their merit will be immeasurable; how much more so for those whom you protect who fully receive and uphold it, making offerings to the scripture with flowers, incense, necklaces, powdered incense, unguents, burning incense, banners, canopies, and music?”

Furthermore, Gautama, those who offer various kinds of lamps—such as ghee lamps, oil lamps, lamps of various fragrant oils, lamps of *sumana* flower oil, lamps of *campaka* flower oil, lamps of *vārṣika* flower oil, and lamps of *utpala* flower oil—in hundreds of thousands of such varieties of offerings; Gautama!
"You and your retinues should protect such Dharma-preachers as these.
When this chapter on the dhāraṇī-mantra was spoken, sixty-eight thousand people attained the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
Chapter Twenty-Two: The Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja At that time, the Bodhisattva Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva, how does he travel through the Sahā world?
World-Honored One!
This Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva has performed hundreds, thousands, tens of millions, billions, nayutas of difficult and painful practices."
Excellent, World-Honored One!
We pray that you will explain this briefly.

The devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, as well as the bodhisattvas who had come from other lands and this assembly of śrāvakas, all rejoiced upon hearing it.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña:

"In the past, immeasurable kalpas ago, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there was a Buddha named Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavat. That Buddha had eight billion great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and a great assembly of Śrāvakas numbering seventy-two times the sands of the Ganges. The lifespan of that Buddha was forty-two thousand kalpas, and the lifespans of the Bodhisattvas were equal to his."

In that land there are no women, nor are there hells, hungry ghosts, animals, asuras, or any of the various calamities. The ground is as level as the palm of a hand, composed of lapis lazuli, and adorned with jeweled trees. Above them are spread jeweled canopies, from which hang jeweled flower banners; jeweled vases and incense burners are distributed throughout the realm.

There are pedestals made of the seven treasures, one for each tree, and the distance between each tree and its pedestal is exactly the range of an arrow-shot. Beneath all these jeweled trees sit bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.
Upon each jeweled pedestal dwell ten billion devas, who perform celestial music and sing praises of the Buddha as an act of offering.
"At that time, that Buddha preached the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* for the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, as well as for the assembly of bodhisattvas and the assembly of śrāvakas."

The Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana delighted in practicing ascetic austerities; within the Dharma of the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, he practiced walking meditation with diligence and sought Buddhahood with single-minded focus for twelve thousand years. Having completed this period, he attained the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms. Upon attaining this samādhi, his heart was filled with great joy, and he thought to himself:

"That I have attained the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms is entirely due to the power of hearing the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. I shall now make offerings to the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī and to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*."

Immediately he entered this samādhi, and from the midst of the void there rained down *māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, and fine powder of black sandalwood, filling the sky and descending like clouds;

furthermore, there rained down the fragrance of *gośīrṣa* sandalwood from the other shore of the ocean—six *zhu* of this incense was worth as much as the entire Sahā world—and with it he made offerings to the Buddha.
"Having made this offering, he arose from samādhi and thought to himself:
'Although I have made offerings to the Buddha through supernatural powers, it is not as good as making an offering with my own body.'"

He then consumed various incenses—sandalwood, frankincense, *turuṣka*, *bhallātaka*, aloeswood, and resin—and also drank the fragrant oils of *campaka* flowers. After twelve hundred years had passed, he anointed his body with fragrant oil and, before the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, wrapped himself in celestial jewel robes and poured over himself fragrant oils. Through the power of his supernatural vows, his body spontaneously blazed forth, its radiance illuminating worlds as numerous as the sands of eight billion Ganges Rivers.
Therein, all the Buddhas simultaneously praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! Well-spoken, son of good family!"
This is true diligence; this is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata.

It cannot be equaled by offerings of flowers, incense, necklaces, burning incense, powdered incense, ointments, celestial silks, banners, canopies, or even the sandalwood from the "this-side-of-the-sea" (jāmbūnada);
nor can it be matched by the giving away of kingdoms, cities, wives, or children.
"Good son! This is called the foremost gift; it is the most honored and supreme among all gifts, because it is an offering of the Dharma to all Tathāgatas."
Having spoken these words, they each became silent.
Their bodies remained ablaze for twelve hundred years, and only after this period had passed were their bodies finally consumed.

After making such offerings of the Dharma, the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana reached the end of his life and was reborn in the land of the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, appearing by transformation in a cross-legged posture within the household of King Śuddhasena.
He then spoke this verse to his father:
"Great King, you should now know: As I was walking there, I immediately attained The Samādhi of Manifesting All Bodies."
"Exerting great diligence, I have renounced my beloved body.
Having spoken this verse, he addressed his father, saying:
"The Buddha Sun-Moon Pure Brightness Virtue still currently exists. Having first made offerings to that Buddha, I attained the *dhāraṇī* for understanding the languages of all sentient beings."
Furthermore, they heard eight hundred thousand million billion nayutas of *khangara*, *bimbala*, and *akṣobhya* verses from this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
"Great King!
I shall now return to make offerings to this Buddha.

Having said this, he immediately sat upon a platform of the seven treasures and ascended into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees. Arriving at the place where the Buddha was, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet and, joining his ten fingers and nails, praised the Buddha with these verses:
“Your countenance is most wondrous and sublime, And your radiance illuminates the ten directions;
I have previously made offerings to you, And now I come once more to behold you in person.”
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana had spoken these verses, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
The World-Honored One still remains in the world."
At that time, the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa said to the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana: "Good son!
The time for my parinirvāṇa has arrived; the moment of my final extinction has come. You should prepare a seat, for tonight I shall enter parinirvāṇa."
He further commanded the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana: "Good son!

I entrust the Buddha-dharma to you and to all the bodhisattvas and great disciples, as well as the Dharma of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. I also entrust to you this trichiliocosm world of seven treasures, including its jeweled trees, jeweled terraces, and the attendant devas."
After my parinirvāṇa, all my relics shall likewise be entrusted to you;
you must cause them to be widely distributed and extensively honored, and you should erect several thousand stūpas.
After the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa had thus instructed the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, he entered parinirvāṇa during the final watch of the night.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, seeing the Buddha’s passing, was overcome with grief and distress, longing for the Buddha. He immediately used *candana* sandalwood from this side of the sea to prepare a pyre, making offerings to the Buddha’s body by cremating it.

After the fire was extinguished, he collected the relics and fashioned eighty-four thousand precious vases, erecting eighty-four thousand stupas. These were three world-systems high, adorned with spires and banners, draped with various canopies, and hung with many jeweled bells.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana again thought to himself:
"Although I have made these offerings, my mind is still not satisfied; I shall now further offer worship to the relics."
He then addressed the assembly of all bodhisattvas, great disciples, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and others:
"You should all focus your minds with single-minded intent:
'I am now making offerings to the relics of the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa.'"

Having spoken these words, he immediately before eighty-four thousand stupas set ablaze his arms, adorned with the marks of a hundred blessings, making offerings for seventy-two thousand years. He caused countless seekers of the śrāvaka vehicle and immeasurable asaṃkhyeya persons to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, enabling them all to abide in the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms.
At that time, the bodhisattvas, devas, humans, asuras, and others, seeing that he was without arms, were filled with grief and sorrow, and spoke these words:
"This Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana is our teacher and the one who instructs us; yet now he has burned his arms, and his body is incomplete."
Then, the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana made this vow before the great assembly:
"I shall sacrifice both my arms; I must surely attain the golden body of a Buddha. If this is true and not false, let my two arms be restored to their former state."
Having made this vow, [the earth] naturally returned to its original state, brought about by the profound thickness of the Bodhisattva’s merit and wisdom.
At that moment, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways, and the heavens rained down precious flowers; all humans and devas attained what they had never experienced before.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Puṣpachatrakūṭarāja: "What do you think?
Is the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana anyone other than this person?"
He is none other than the present Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
The manner in which he sacrificed his body as an act of giving was such that it occurred countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of times.
"O Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña!..."

If there is one who resolves to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and is able to offer their finger, or even a single toe, as an offering to a Buddha-stūpa, this surpasses one who offers kingdoms, cities, wives, children, and the mountains, forests, rivers, lakes, and all manner of rare treasures within a trichiliocosm.

Furthermore, if there were a person who filled the three-thousandfold world system with the seven treasures and offered them as alms to the Buddhas, great Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Arhats, the merit obtained by that person would not equal the merit of one who receives, upholds, and recites even a single four-line verse of this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*; the latter’s blessings are far greater.
Ratnakusumavikrāmin!
Just as, among all streams, rivers, and waters, the ocean is foremost;
so too is this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, for it is the most profound and vast among all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas.

Furthermore, just as among all mountains—the Earth Mountains, the Black Mountains, the Lesser Iron Ring Mountains, the Great Iron Ring Mountains, and the Ten Treasure Mountains—Mount Sumeru is the foremost;
so too is this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, which is the most supreme among all sūtras.
Furthermore, just as among all the stars the Moon Deity is the most preeminent, so too is this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*;
among the hundreds of thousands of millions of various sūtras and dharmas, it is the most illuminating.
Furthermore, just as the Sun Deva is able to dispel all darkness, so too is this sutra, which can shatter the darkness of all that is unwholesome.
Again, just as among all minor kings, the Wheel-Turning Sage King is the most preeminent; so it is with this sutra.
This sutra is likewise so; among all sutras, it is the most honored.
Furthermore, just as Śakra is the king among the thirty-three gods, this sutra is likewise the king among all sutras.
Furthermore, just as Mahābrahmā is the father of all sentient beings,
so too is this sutra the father of all noble ones— those in training (*śaikṣa*), those beyond training (*aśaikṣa*), and those who have resolved to attain the mind of a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, just as among all ordinary persons, the *srotāpanna*, *sakṛdāgāmin*, *anāgāmin*, *arhat*, and *pratyekabuddha* are the foremost;
so too is this sutra: among all the teachings spoken by the Tathāgatas, those spoken by bodhisattvas, or those spoken by śrāvakas, it is the most supreme.
One who is able to receive and uphold this sutra is likewise so; among all sentient beings, they are also the foremost.
Among all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, the bodhisattva is the foremost;
this sutra is also like this, being the most supreme among all sūtras and dharmas.
Just as the Buddha is the king of all dharmas,
so too is this sutra the king among all sutras.
"O Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña!

This sutra can save all sentient beings; this sutra can cause all sentient beings to leave behind all suffering and affliction; this sutra can greatly benefit all sentient beings and fulfill their aspirations. It is like a cool pond that can satisfy all those who are parched with thirst; it is like a cold person finding fire, like a naked person finding clothing, like a merchant finding his master, like a child finding its mother, like one crossing water finding a boat, like a sick person finding a physician, like one in darkness finding a lamp, like a poor person finding treasure, like a subject finding a king, like a merchant finding the sea, and like a torch dispelling darkness.
This *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* is also like this: it can cause sentient beings to leave behind all suffering and all ailments, and it can untie all the bonds of birth and death.

If a person hears this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, whether they write it themselves or cause others to write it, the merit they obtain is such that even if one were to measure its extent with the wisdom of a Buddha, one could not reach its limit.

If one writes out this sutra scroll and makes offerings with flowers, incense, necklaces, burnt incense, powdered incense, ointment incense, banners, canopies, and robes, as well as various kinds of lamps—such as ghee lamps, oil lamps, lamps of various fragrant oils, lamps of *campaka* oil, *sumanā* oil, *pāṭala* oil, *bharuṣka* oil, and *nāgamallī* oil—the merit obtained will likewise be immeasurable.
“Ratnapuṣpa! If there are those who hear this ‘Chapter on the Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,’ they too shall attain immeasurable and boundless merit.”

If there are women who, upon hearing this "Chapter on the Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja," are able to receive and uphold it, they shall exhaust their female bodies and never again assume them hereafter.

If, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, during the final five hundred years, there should be a woman who hears this sutra and practices according to its teaching, at the end of her life she will immediately go to the World of Peace and Bliss, to the dwelling place of Amitābha Buddha surrounded by a multitude of great bodhisattvas. She will be born within a lotus flower upon a jeweled throne; she will no longer be afflicted by desire, nor afflicted by anger or ignorance, nor afflicted by the defilements of pride, jealousy, and the like. She will attain the supernatural powers of a bodhisattva and the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Having attained this patience, their faculty of the eye becomes pure; with this purified faculty of the eye, they see seven million two thousand *koṭi-nayuta* Ganges-sand-like Buddhas, Tathāgatas.
At that time, all the Buddhas praised him from afar, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! O son of good family!"

That you are able, within the Dharma of Śākyamuni Buddha, to receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, and explain this sutra for others—your resulting merit will be immeasurable and boundless; fire cannot burn it, and water cannot sweep it away. Your merit is such that even if a thousand Buddhas were to speak of it together, they could not exhaust it. You have now been able to defeat the thieves of Māra, destroy the army of birth and death, and utterly crush all other enemies.

"Good son! Hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, by means of their supernormal powers, together protect you. Among all the devas and humans in every world, there is no one like you, with the sole exception of the Tathāgata."
"Among all those śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and even bodhisattvas, there is none whose wisdom or meditative concentration equals yours.
"O Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña!"

When this Bodhisattva has accomplished such power of merit and wisdom, if there are those who hear this "Chapter on the Past Deeds of Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva" and are able to rejoice in it and praise it as good, that person will, in their present life, constantly have the fragrance of blue lotuses issue from their mouth, and the fragrance of ox-head sandalwood will constantly issue from the pores of their body; the merit they obtain shall be as described above.
Therefore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña!

I entrust this "Chapter on the Past Deeds of Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja" to you. After my parinirvāṇa, during the final five hundred years, you must propagate and disseminate it widely throughout Jambudvīpa so that it shall not be interrupted, lest evil Māras, their followers, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others find an opportunity to cause harm.
Ratnakusuma! You should, by means of your supernormal powers, protect this sutra. Why is that?

This sutra is the excellent medicine for the illnesses of the people of Jambudvīpa; if anyone has an illness and hears this sutra, their disease will be immediately extinguished, and they shall neither grow old nor die.
Rājanpuṣpa! If you see anyone who upholds this sutra, you should take blue lotuses filled with powdered incense and scatter them over that person. Having scattered them, you should form this thought:

"This person will, before long, surely take grass and sit at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) to shatter the armies of Māra; they shall blow the Dharma conch and beat the great Dharma drum, delivering all sentient beings from the ocean of old age, sickness, and death."
"Therefore, those who seek the Buddha-way, upon seeing anyone who receives and upholds this sutra, should give rise to a heart of reverence such as this.
When this "Chapter on the Past Deeds of Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva" was being preached, eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas attained the dhāraṇī for understanding the languages of all sentient beings.
From within the precious stupa, the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna praised the Bodhisattva Rājādhiṣṭhānavaśavartin,
saying: "Excellent, excellent, Rājādhiṣṭhānavaśavartin!"
You have accomplished inconceivable merit, being able to inquire of Śākyamuni Buddha about such matters as these, thereby benefiting immeasurable sentient beings.
