Chapter Twenty-Three: The Chapter on the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara.

At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha emitted the radiance from the *uṣṇīṣa*—the mark of a Great Man—and emitted the light from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows, which shone throughout one hundred and eight million *nayuta* Ganges-sand-like Buddha-worlds in the eastern direction.

Beyond this number of worlds, there is a world named Pure Light Adornment (*Vimalaprabhā-vyūha*). In that land dwells a Buddha named Pure Flower Constellation King Wisdom Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One. He is surrounded by a great assembly of immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas, who pay him respectful homage as he preaches the Dharma for them.
The light from the white tuft of hair between the eyebrows of Śākyamuni Buddha shone throughout that land.
At that time, in the land of Universal Purity and Radiant Adornment, there was a bodhisattva named Gadgadasvara,
who had long since planted the roots of manifold virtues and had made offerings to and drawn near countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddhas.
And they have all fully accomplished profound wisdom, attaining the Samādhi of the Wondrous Banner, the Lotus Sūtra Samādhi, the Samādhi of Pure Virtue,
the Samādhi of the Constellation King’s Play, the Samādhi of No-Condition, the Samādhi of the Seal of Wisdom,
the Samādhi of Understanding the Languages of All Sentient Beings, and the Samādhi of Accumulating All Meritorious Virtues.
...the Samādhi of Purity, the Samādhi of Playful Mastery of Supernatural Powers, the Samādhi of the Torch of Wisdom, the Samādhi of the King of Adornments,
the Samādhi of Pure Radiance, the Samādhi of the Pure Treasury, the Unshared Samādhi, the Sun-Spinning Samādhi,
and hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of such great samādhis, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
In his state of mental darkness, Śākyamuni Buddha’s light shone upon his body, and he addressed the Buddha Pure Flower Constellation King Wisdom, saying:
“World-Honored One!...”

I shall go to the Sahā world to pay homage, draw near to, and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha, and to see the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, as well as the Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja, Sūradatta, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumita, Viśiṣṭacāritra, Vyūharāja, and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata.
At that time, the Buddha Śubhavyūha-rāja-saṃkusumitābhijña addressed the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara:
“Go, noble son; do not disparage that land by conceiving thoughts of inferiority. Noble son!...”

That Sahā world is uneven with highs and lows, filled with mountains of earth and stone and all manner of impurities; the Buddha’s body is short and small, and the forms of the assembly of bodhisattvas are likewise small. Your body is forty-two thousand yojanas in height, while my body is six million eight hundred thousand yojanas; your body is preeminent in its beauty, with hundreds of thousands of millions of meritorious radiances most exquisite. Therefore, when you go there, do not disparage that land, nor conceive thoughts of inferiority toward the Buddha, the bodhisattvas, or the realm.
The Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara addressed his Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
That I now journey to the Sahā world is entirely through the power of the Tathāgata, the playful mastery of the Tathāgata’s supernormal powers, and the adornment of the Tathāgata’s merit and wisdom."

Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara, without rising from his seat and without his body moving, entered a samādhi. By the power of that samādhi, not far from the Dharma-seat on Vulture Peak Mountain, he manifested eighty-four thousand lotus flowers made of various jewels, with stems of Jāmbūnada gold, petals of white silver, filaments of diamond, and pericarps of kimsuka gems.
At that time, the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, seeing these lotuses, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

By what causes and conditions has this auspicious omen first appeared, such that there are many tens of millions of lotuses with stems of Jāmbūnada gold, leaves of white silver, filaments of diamond, and pericarps made of kiṃśuka jewels?”
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed Mañjuśrī:

“This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara wishes to come from the land of the Buddha Śubhavyūharāja to this Sahā world, surrounded by eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas, in order to make offerings to, draw near to, and pay homage to me; he also wishes to make offerings to and listen to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.”
Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
What roots of goodness has this bodhisattva planted, and what merits has he cultivated, that he is able to possess such great supernormal powers?"
"What samādhi do you practice?

We pray that you will tell us the name of this samādhi; we also wish to diligently cultivate its practice. By practicing this samādhi, we shall be able to see the physical appearance, dimensions, and the dignified deportment and movements of this bodhisattva."
“I only pray that the World-Honored One, by means of your supernormal powers, will cause that Bodhisattva to come so that I may behold him.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed Mañjuśrī:
“This Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, who entered parinirvāṇa long ago, shall now manifest his form for your sake.”
Then the Buddha Prabhūtaratna addressed that bodhisattva:
"Good son, come! The Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī wishes to see you."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara vanished from that land and set out together with eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas. As they passed through various lands, the earth shook in six ways, showers of seven-jeweled lotuses fell everywhere, and hundreds of thousands of celestial musical instruments played spontaneously without being struck.
This Bodhisattva’s eyes are like the broad petals of a great blue lotus; even if a hundred thousand million moons were brought together, his countenance would be more upright and handsome than they.

His body is of true golden color, adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of merits; his majestic virtue is blazing and his radiance shines forth, as he is fully endowed with all the marks [of a Great Man].
Like the firm body of Nārāyaṇa, he enters a pavilion of the seven treasures and ascends into the void, rising seven *tāla* trees above the ground.
Surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattvas who paid him respectful homage, he came to this Sahā world, to Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa.

Upon arrival, he descended from his seven-jeweled terrace and, taking a necklace worth hundreds of thousands, went to where Śākyamuni Buddha was. Prostrating with his head at the Buddha’s feet, he presented the necklace and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!...”
The Buddha Śubhavyūharājasaṃkusumitābhijña inquires after the World-Honored One: Are you free from illness and affliction? Is your daily life light and easy, and do you dwell in peace and happiness?
Are the four great elements in harmony?
"Can the affairs of the world be endured?
Are sentient beings easy to deliver?
Do they not have excessive greed, anger, delusion, envy, stinginess, or arrogance?"
Are you not unfilial toward your parents? Are you not disrespectful toward śramaṇas?
Do you have no wrong views?
Do you have no unwholesome thoughts?
"Does he restrain the five sense-faculties?
World-Honored One!
Are sentient beings able to subdue all maras and enemies?"
"Has the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, who entered parinirvāṇa long ago, come from within his stupa made of the seven precious substances to hear the Dharma?
Furthermore, inquire after the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna’s welfare: whether he is at ease, free from affliction, and able to endure for a long time?"
“World-Honored One!
I now wish to see the body of the Buddha Prabhūtaratna; I only pray that the World-Honored One will show it to me so that I may behold it.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha spoke to the Buddha Prabhūtaratna:
"This Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara wishes to meet you.
At that time, the Buddha Prabhūtaratna addressed Gadgadasvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"You have come here for the sake of making offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha, for listening to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, and for seeing Mañjuśrī and the others.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Flower Virtue addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What roots of goodness has this Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara planted, and what merits has he cultivated, that he possesses such supernatural power?
The Buddha told Flower Virtue Bodhisattva:

"In the past, there was a Buddha named Cloud Thunder Sound King (*Meghadundubhisvararāja*), a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. His land was named Manifesting All Worlds, and his eon was named Joyful Sight."

For twelve thousand years, the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara made offerings of one hundred thousand kinds of music to the Buddha Meghadundubhisvararāja, and further presented eighty-four thousand bowls made of the seven precious substances. By virtue of these causes and conditions and their karmic retribution, he has now been born in the presence of the Buddha Śubhavyūha-rājanarendrayaśas and possesses such supernormal powers.
Śrīguṇarāja! What do you think?
Was the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara—who at that time, in the presence of the Buddha Ghoṣadatta-rāja, made offerings of music and presented precious vessels—anyone else?
This is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara.
Flower Virtue!

This Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara has already made offerings to and drawn near countless Buddhas, long planting the roots of merit, and has further encountered hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Śubhavyūha! You see only that the body of the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara is here;
however, this Bodhisattva manifests various bodies, everywhere preaching this sutra for the sake of all sentient beings—sometimes manifesting as the body of a Brahmā King, or sometimes manifesting...
He may manifest as the body of Śakra, or manifest as the body of Īśvara, or manifest as the body of Maheśvara, or manifest as the body of a celestial general,
or manifest as the body of Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King, or manifest as the body of a universal monarch (cakravartin),
or manifest as the body of various minor kings, or manifest as the body of a householder, or manifest as the body of a lay devotee.
In bodily form, he may manifest as a minister, or as a brahmin, or as a bhikṣu, bhikṣuṇī, upāsaka, or upāsikā; or he may manifest as an elder, a lay devotee, or a woman;
or he may manifest as the wife of a minister, or as the wife of a brahmin.
With his body, he may manifest in the form of a boy or a girl, or manifest in the forms of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras,
mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth, while preaching this sūtra.

They are able to rescue and deliver all those in the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, as well as those in various places of suffering; even within the royal harem, they manifest in female form to preach this sutra.
Śubhavyūha! This Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara is one who can rescue and protect all sentient beings in the Sahā world.

This Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara manifests various such transformations of his body here in this Sahā land to preach this sutra for the sake of all sentient beings; yet, in his supernormal powers, transformations, and wisdom, there is no diminution whatsoever.

This Bodhisattva, with various forms of wisdom, illuminates the Sahā world, causing all sentient beings to each attain what they need to know; it is likewise so throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions. To those who should be delivered by appearing in the form of a Śrāvaka, he manifests in the form of a Śrāvaka and preaches the Dharma for them;
to those who should be delivered by appearing in the form of a Pratyekabuddha, he manifests in the form of a Pratyekabuddha and preaches the Dharma for them;
to those who should be delivered by appearing in the form of a Bodhisattva, he manifests in the form of a Bodhisattva and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who should be saved by the form of a Buddha, he manifests the form of a Buddha and preaches the Dharma for them;
in this way, he manifests various forms according to the needs of those to be saved.
Even for those who are to be delivered through parinirvāṇa, he manifests parinirvāṇa. Flower Virtue!
Such are the deeds of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, who has accomplished the power of great supernormal knowledges and wisdom.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Flower Virtue addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Bodhisattva Wonderful Sound has deeply planted roots of goodness.”
“World-Honored One!
In what samādhi does this bodhisattva abide, such that he is able to manifest transformations in all places to deliver and liberate sentient beings?
The Buddha addressed Flower Virtue Bodhisattva:
“Good son! That samādhi is named ‘Manifesting All Physical Bodies’;
by abiding in this samādhi, the Bodhisattva Wonderful Sound is able to benefit immeasurable sentient beings in such a manner.”

When this "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara" was being preached, the eighty-four thousand people who had come together with the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara all attained the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms. Furthermore, immeasurable bodhisattvas in this Sahā world also attained this samādhi as well as dhāraṇīs.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, having made offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha and the stupa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha, returned to his own land. As he passed through various countries, the earth shook in six ways, precious lotus flowers rained down, and hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kinds of music were played.
Having arrived in his own land, surrounded by eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas, he went to the place where the Buddha Pure Flower Constellation King Wisdom was and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
I have come to the Sahā world to benefit sentient beings; I have seen Śākyamuni Buddha and the stupa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha, where I paid homage and made offerings.

I also saw the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, as well as Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva, Vīryadattabala Bodhisattva, Sūradatta Bodhisattva, and others, and have likewise enabled these eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas to attain the Samādhi of Manifesting All Physical Forms.

When this "Chapter on the Coming and Going of the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara" was being preached, forty-two thousand devaputras attained the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), and the bodhisattva Puṣpadatta attained the Lotus Samādhi (*Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi*).

Chapter Twenty-Four: The Universal Gate of Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. From the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, the "Supplementary Chapter. At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what causes and conditions is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara named 'Observer of the Sounds of the World'?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati: "Good son!"

If there are immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of sentient beings undergoing various sufferings and afflictions, and they hear of this Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and single-mindedly invoke his name, "Avalokiteśvara," then immediately upon hearing their voices, he shall cause them all to attain liberation.

"If there be anyone who holds the name of this Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, even if they enter a great fire, the fire shall not burn them, by virtue of the majestic spiritual power of this Bodhisattva."
"If one is being swept away by a great flood, by invoking his name, one will immediately find shallow ground.

If there are hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, millions, or billions of sentient beings who enter the great ocean seeking treasures such as gold, silver, lapis lazuli, musaragalva, agate, coral, amber, and pearls—"

Even if a black wind should blow their ship and cast it adrift into the land of the rākṣasa demons, if among those on board there is even a single person who calls upon the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, all of them shall be liberated from the peril of the rākṣasas.
For these reasons, he is named Avalokiteśvara.

Furthermore, if there is anyone who is about to be harmed and invokes the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the swords and staves held by their assailants will immediately shatter into pieces, and they shall obtain liberation.

"If yakṣas and rākṣasas should fill a trichiliocosm and wish to come and harass people, upon hearing them invoke the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, these evil spirits would not even be able to look upon them with malevolent eyes, let alone inflict harm."

"Furthermore, if there are people—whether guilty or innocent—who have their bodies bound by cangues, fetters, stocks, or shackles, should they invoke the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, all such restraints will be broken and destroyed, and they shall immediately attain liberation."

"Suppose that throughout a trichiliocosm world-system there were bandits and thieves filling every part, and a certain caravan leader, leading many merchants and carrying heavy treasures, was traveling along a perilous road."
One among them spoke these words:
"O virtuous sons! Do not be afraid!"

"You all should single-mindedly invoke the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; this Bodhisattva is able to bestow fearlessness upon sentient beings, and if you invoke his name, you shall attain liberation from these hostile bandits."
Upon hearing this, all the merchants cried out with one voice,
"Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva!
By invoking his name, they immediately attained liberation.
“Akṣayamati! The majestic spiritual power of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara is as sublime as this.
If there are sentient beings who abound in lustful desire, and they constantly keep Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva in mind with reverence, they shall immediately become free from desire.”
If one is prone to much anger, by constantly recollecting and reverently honoring Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one will immediately become free from anger.
If one is prone to much delusion, by constantly recollecting and reverently honoring Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one will immediately become free from delusion.
Akṣayamati! The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara possesses such great majestic spiritual power and brings benefit to many.
For this reason, sentient beings should constantly keep him in mind.
"If there is a woman who wishes to give birth to a son, and she pays homage with reverence to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, she shall give birth to a son endowed with merit and wisdom;

if she wishes to give birth to a daughter, she shall give birth to a daughter who is upright and possesses auspicious marks, one who has planted the roots of virtue in past lives and is loved and respected by all."
“Akṣayamati! The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara possesses such power.
If there are sentient beings who pay respect and prostrate to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, their merit shall not be in vain.”
Therefore, all sentient beings should receive and uphold the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. "Akṣayamati!

Suppose there were someone who received and upheld the names of sixty-two billion Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and further provided them with offerings of food, drink, clothing, bedding, and medicine for as long as they lived—what do you think?"
"Would these sons and daughters of good family have much merit? Ajita said, "Very much!"
“World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“If there is another person who receives and upholds the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, even for a single moment bowing in worship and making offerings, the merit of these two persons is exactly equal and without difference, and it cannot be exhausted throughout hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of kalpas.”
“Akṣayamati! By upholding the name of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, one obtains such immeasurable and boundless benefits of merit.
The Bodhisattva Akṣayamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara traverse this Sahā world?
How does he preach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings?”
"What is the nature of the power of skillful means?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati: "Good son!..."

If there are sentient beings in any land who are to be liberated by means of a Buddha’s body, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva immediately manifests in the form of a Buddha and preaches the Dharma for them.
If there are those who are to be liberated by means of a Pratyekabuddha’s body, he immediately manifests in the form of a Pratyekabuddha and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who should be delivered by means of the body of a śrāvaka, he manifests the body of a śrāvaka and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who should be delivered by means of the body of a Brahmā king, he manifests the body of a Brahmā king and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who should be liberated by means of the body of Śakra, he manifests the body of Śakra and preaches the Dharma to them.
To those who should be liberated by means of the body of Īśvara, he manifests the body of Īśvara and preaches the Dharma to them.
To those who should be liberated by means of the body of Maheśvara, he manifests the body of Maheśvara and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who should be liberated by means of the body of a celestial general, he manifests the body of a celestial general and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who should be liberated through the form of Vaiśravaṇa, he manifests as Vaiśravaṇa and preaches the Dharma to them.
To those who should be liberated through the form of a minor king, he manifests as a minor king and preaches the Dharma to them.
To those who should be saved by the body of a householder, he manifests in the body of a householder and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who should be saved by the body of a lay devotee, he manifests in the body of a lay devotee and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who are to be saved by means of the body of a minister, he manifests in the body of a minister and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who are to be saved by means of the body of a Brahmin, he manifests in the body of a Brahmin and preaches the Dharma for them.

To those who are to be delivered by means of the bodies of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, he immediately manifests the body of a bhikṣu, bhikṣuṇī, upāsaka, or upāsikā and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who should be delivered by means of the bodies of elders, householders, officials, brahmins, or women, he immediately manifests in the body of a woman and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who are to be liberated through the form of a young boy or a young girl, he immediately manifests the body of a young boy or a young girl and preaches the Dharma for them.

To those who are to be liberated through the forms of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth, he immediately manifests all such forms and preaches the Dharma for them.
To those who are to be saved by the Vajrapāṇi deity, he manifests as the Vajrapāṇi deity and preaches the Dharma for them.
"Akṣayamati! The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara has accomplished such meritorious virtues; assuming various forms, he travels through all lands to deliver sentient beings."
Therefore, you all should with one mind make offerings to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
This Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara is able to bestow fearlessness amidst terrors and urgent perils; for this reason, throughout this Sahā world, he is universally known as the "Bestower of Fearlessness."
The Bodhisattva Akṣayamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I shall now make offerings to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.”
He immediately untied a necklace of various precious jewels from his neck, worth hundreds of thousands of taels of gold, and gave it to him, saying:
"Virtuous one! Accept this precious jewel necklace as a gift of Dharma."
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva was unwilling to accept it.
Then, Akṣayamati addressed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva again, saying:
"O Benevolent One!
"Out of compassion for us, please accept this necklace.
At that time, the Buddha told Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva:

"Out of compassion for this Akṣayamati Bodhisattva, as well as for the fourfold assembly, and the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, you should accept this necklace."

Thereupon, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, out of compassion for the fourfold assembly as well as the devas, nāgas, humans, and non-humans, accepted the necklace and divided it into two portions: one portion he offered to Śākyamuni Buddha, and the other portion he offered to the stupa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha.
“Akṣayamati! The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara possesses such sovereign spiritual powers as these as he wanders through the Sahā world.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vyūhadhvaja addressed the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, saying:
“Sons of the Buddha!
For what reason is he named Avalokiteśvara?
Bodhisattva Akṣayamati then surveyed throughout the ocean of past vows of Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and addressed Bodhisattva Vyūhadhvaja, saying:
“O Son of the Buddha!
Listen attentively to the practices performed by the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati spoke these verses:
“The World-Honored One, endowed with wondrous marks, I now ask you again:
For what cause and condition, O Son of the Buddha, is he named Avalokiteśvara?
The Honored One, fully possessed of wondrous marks, answered Akṣayamati in verse.
Listen now to the practice of Avalokiteśvara, Who skillfully responds to all places and circumstances.
His great vows are as deep as the ocean, Spun over inconceivable eons;
He has served many thousands of billions of Buddhas, And made vast, pure aspirations.
I shall briefly explain for you: hearing his name, seeing his body, or bringing him to mind—none of these pass in vain;
they can extinguish all suffering within the realms of existence.
Even if one were to harbor malice and push another into a great pit of fire;
By recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, a fiery pit is transformed into a pool.
Or if one is drifting upon the vast ocean, beset by the perils of fish, dragons, and various ghosts;
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, the surging waves cannot submerge them.
Or if one were on the peak of Mount Sumeru, pushed over by others;
by virtue of recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, one would remain in the sky like the sun.
Or if pursued by evil men, one might fall down upon the Diamond Mountains;
By recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, not even a single hair can be harmed.
Even if one encounters hostile bandits surrounding them, each wielding a blade to inflict injury;
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, they all immediately give rise to a heart of compassion.
Should one encounter the suffering of royal persecution, On the verge of execution as life draws to its end;
If they call upon the power of Avalokiteśvara, The blade shall instantly break into pieces.
Or if imprisoned and bound with shackles, With hands and feet fettered by cangues and manacles;
By recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, one attains liberation with ease.
As for those who cast curses and various poisons, wishing to harm the body—
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, they shall immediately turn back and depart.
Should one encounter evil rākṣasas, venomous dragons, various ghosts, and the like;
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, they shall all dare not cause harm at that time.
Even if surrounded by fierce beasts with terrifying sharp fangs and claws;
By recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, one flees swiftly to boundless directions.
Even when vipers, snakes, and scorpions emit poisonous vapors like blazing smoke and fire,
by recollecting the power of Avalokiteśvara, they turn back of their own accord upon hearing the voice.
When clouds and thunder roll, lightning flashes, hail falls, and great rains pour down;
by calling upon the power of Avalokiteśvara, they shall be dispersed in an instant.
When sentient beings are beset by calamities and oppressed by immeasurable suffering;
The wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom can rescue the world from suffering.
Endowed with the power of supernormal faculties and having extensively cultivated wisdom and skillful means,
there is no land throughout the worlds of the ten directions in which he does not manifest his body.
The various evil realms—hell, hungry ghosts, and animals;
The sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death— He causes them all to be gradually extinguished.
True contemplation, pure contemplation, And the contemplation of vast wisdom;
With contemplations of compassion and loving-kindness, I always aspire and gaze upward.
With stainless, pure radiance, the sun of wisdom shatters all darkness;
it can subdue the winds and fires of calamity, shining universally upon the world.
The thunderous roar of the precepts, whose essence is compassion; the wondrous great cloud of a benevolent mind—showering down the nectar-rain of the Dharma, it extinguishes the flames of affliction.
Whether in legal disputes before government officials or amidst the terrors of battle arrays;
By recollecting the power of that Avalokiteśvara, all enemies shall retreat and disperse.
With his wondrous voice, his voice that observes the world, his Brahma-voice, and his ocean-tide voice—
surpassing all worldly sounds— one should therefore always keep him in mind.
In every thought-moment, do not give rise to doubt; Avalokiteśvara is a pure and holy one.
Amidst suffering, affliction, and the perils of death, he is able to act as a refuge.
Possessing all meritorious virtues, he gazes upon sentient beings with eyes of compassion.
"The ocean of merit is immeasurable; therefore, one should pay homage with the crown of the head.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharaṇīdhara rose from his seat, approached the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If there are sentient beings who hear this "Chapter on Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva" regarding his sovereign deeds and the supernormal powers manifested through the Universal Door, you should know that the merit of such persons is not small.

When the Buddha preached this "Universal Gate" chapter, eighty-four thousand sentient beings among the assembly all gave rise to the mind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, which is peerless.
Chapter Twenty-five: The Past Deeds of King Wonderful Adornment. At that time, the Buddha addressed the great assembly:

"In the distant past, beyond immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there was a Buddha named Cloud-Thunder-Sound-Constellation-King-Flower-Wisdom (*Meghadundubhisvararājaketudhvaja-jñāna*), a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. His land was named Radiant Adornment (*Prabhāvyūha*), and his eon was named Joyful Vision (*Priyadarśana*).
In that Buddha-dharma, there was a king named Wondrous Adornment; his queen was named Pure Virtue, and they had two sons:
the first was named Pure Treasury, and the second was named Pure Eye.

These two sons possess great supernormal powers, merit, and wisdom; they have long cultivated the path practiced by bodhisattvas—namely, the dāna-pāramitā, śīla-pāramitā, kṣānti-pāramitā, vīrya-pāramitā, dhyāna-pāramitā, prajñā-pāramitā, and upāya-pāramitā—as well as loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, up to and including the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment—all of which they have fully understood and mastered.

Furthermore, he attained the Bodhisattva’s Pure Samādhi, the Sun and Stars Samādhi, the Pure Light Samādhi, the Pure Color Samādhi, the Pure Illumination Samādhi, the Long Adornment Samādhi, and the Great Majestic Virtue Treasury Samādhi; he also fully mastered all these samādhis.
"At that time, that Buddha, wishing to guide King Subhavyūha and out of compassion for sentient beings, preached this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
Then the two sons, Viśuddhagarbha and Viśuddhanetra, went to their mother’s place, joined their palms with ten fingers together, and said:
'We pray that you, Mother, will go to the place of the Buddha Meghadundubhisvararājasaṃkusumitābhijña; we too shall attend upon, behold, make offerings to, and prostrate before him.'"
"Why is this? This Buddha, amidst the assembly of all devas and humans, is preaching the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*; you ought to listen to and receive it.
The mother said to her son:
"Your father believes in and accepts the teachings of external paths and is deeply attached to the Brahmanical dharma; you should go and inform your father so that we may go together.
Then, with their ten fingers joined in palms, Pure Treasury and Pure Eye said to their mother:
"We are sons of the Dharma King, yet we have been born into this family of false views."
The mother said to her sons:

"You should concern yourselves with your father by manifesting a supernatural transformation for him; if he should see it, his mind will surely become pure, or else you may allow us to go to where the Buddha is."

Thereupon, out of concern for their father, the two sons leaped into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees and manifested various supernatural transformations. They walked, stood, sat, and lay down in mid-air; water issued from the upper part of their bodies while fire issued from the lower parts, and fire issued from the lower parts while water issued from the upper parts.
They manifested a massive body that filled the sky and then became small again, or became large again after being small.
Vanishing from the air, they suddenly reappeared on the ground.

Entering the earth as if it were water and treading upon water as if it were solid ground, he manifested such various supernatural transformations that his father, the king, attained pure faith and understanding.
Seeing his son’s spiritual power thus displayed, the father was filled with great joy at having experienced something unprecedented; joining his palms toward his son, he said: "Who is your teacher?"
"Whose disciple are you?
The two sons replied, "Great King!"

That Buddha, Cloud-Thunder-Sound-Constellation-King-Flower-Wisdom, is now seated upon the Dharma throne beneath a bodhi tree made of the seven precious substances. In the midst of all the multitudes of devas and humans throughout the world, he is extensively preaching the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. He is our teacher, and we are his disciples.
The father said to his sons, "I now also wish to see your teachers; let us go together.
Thereupon, the two sons descended from the sky to where their mother was, joined their palms, and addressed her:

"Since our father the King has now attained faith and understanding and is capable of resolving to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, we have fulfilled our filial duty toward him as Buddhas. We pray that our mother will grant us permission to leave the household life and cultivate the Way under that Buddha."
At that time, the two sons, wishing to restate their intention, addressed their mother in verse:
“May our mother release us, so that we may leave the home life and become śramaṇas;
for Buddhas are extremely difficult to encounter, and we shall follow the Buddha to study.”
“As rare as the udumbara flower, so too is it difficult to encounter a Buddha;
even more difficult is it to be liberated from all perils. I pray that you will grant me permission to leave the household life.
Her mother then said to her:
"I grant you permission to leave the household life. Why is this?
Because a Buddha is difficult to encounter."
Then the two sons said to their parents: "Excellent, parents!
We pray that you will go at once to the presence of the Buddha Cloud-Thunder-Sound Sovereign King Flower-Wisdom to behold him in person and make offerings."
Why is this? Because a Buddha is difficult to encounter, as rare as the udumbara flower;
or like a one-eyed turtle encountering the hole in a floating log. Yet we, through the profound depth of our past merit, have been born into the presence of the Buddha’s Dharma.
Therefore, parents, you should grant us permission to leave the household life.
Why is this? Because Buddhas are difficult to encounter, and their appearance in the world is likewise rare.
“At that time, the eighty-four thousand women in the inner palace of King Wonderful Adornment were all capable of receiving and upholding this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.”
The Bodhisattva Viśuddhanetra has long since attained mastery in the Lotus Samādhi.

The Bodhisattva Viśuddhagarbha has, throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, attained mastery in the Samādhi of Departing from All Evil Destinies, desiring to cause all sentient beings to leave behind all evil destinies.

The king’s consort had attained the Samādhi of the Assembly of All Buddhas and was able to know the secret treasury of all Buddhas. In this way, the two sons used the power of skillful means to skillfully transform their father, causing his mind to develop faith and understanding, and to take delight in the Buddha-dharma.

Thereupon, King Wonderful Adornment, together with his ministers and retinue; Lady Pure Virtue, together with her ladies-in-waiting and retinue; and the king’s two sons, together with forty-two thousand people, all went at once to the place where the Buddha was. Having arrived, they bowed their heads at his feet in prostration, circumambulated the Buddha three times, and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, that Buddha preached the Dharma for the king, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening him, until the king was filled with great joy.

Then King Subhavyūha and his queen took off from their necks pearl necklaces worth hundreds of thousands and scattered them over the Buddha; in mid-air, these transformed into a precious four-pillared pavilion. Within the pavilion was a great jeweled throne, spread with hundreds of thousands of millions of celestial robes. Upon it sat the Buddha in the full lotus posture, emitting a great radiance.
At that time, King Subhavyūha had this thought:
"The Buddha’s body is rare and marvelous, upright, dignified, and extraordinary, having accomplished the foremost and most subtle of forms."
Then the Buddha Meghadundubhisvararāja-pūrvayugaśrīcūḍabuddhi addressed the fourfold assembly, saying:
"Do you see this King Subhavyūha standing before me with palms joined?"

This king shall become a bhikṣu within my Dharma, diligently cultivating the dharmas that assist the path to Buddhahood; he shall attain buddhahood, named Śālarājā, with a land called Mahāprabha and an eon named Mahocchrayarāja.
"The Buddha Śālarāja has an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas and an immeasurable number of śrāvakas; his land is level and upright, and its merits are such as these.

Thereupon, the king immediately entrusted the kingdom to his younger brother and, together with his consort, two sons, and all his retinue, went forth from home to practice the Way within the Buddha-dharma.

“After the king had renounced the world, he constantly applied himself with diligent vigor for eighty-four thousand years, practicing the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*. Following this period, he attained the Samādhi Adorned with All Pure Merits.”
He immediately ascended into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

These two sons of mine have already performed the work of a Buddha; by means of their supernatural transformations, they have turned back my perverse mind, enabling me to dwell securely within the Buddha-dharma and to behold the World-Honored One."
"These two sons are my spiritual friends; desiring to arouse the roots of goodness from past lives and to benefit me, they have been born into my household.
At that time, the Buddha Cloud-Thunder-Sound-Constellation-King-Flower-Wisdom said to King Subhavyūha: "So it is, so it is!"
It is as you have said.

If good sons or good daughters, by virtue of having planted roots of goodness, encounter spiritual friends from lifetime to lifetime—those spiritual friends who are able to perform the work of a Buddha, instructing, teaching, benefiting, and gladdening them, causing them to enter into *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

"Great King, you should know that a virtuous friend is a great causal condition; that is to say, they transform and guide one so that one may see the Buddha and resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi."
"Great King!
Do you see these two sons?

These two sons have already made offerings to sixty-five hundred thousand million billion nayutas of Ganges-sands of Buddhas, personally beholding and revering them; under those Buddhas, they upheld the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, and out of compassion for sentient beings with false views, they established them in right view."
"King Wondrous Adornment immediately descended from mid-air and addressed the Buddha, saying: 'World-Honored One! The Tathāgata is most rare and extraordinary;

by virtue of his merit and wisdom, the light from the *uṣṇīṣa* on the crown of his head shines forth brilliantly. His eyes are long and wide, of a deep blue-black color; the tuft of hair between his brows is as white as a conch or the moon; his teeth are white, even, and closely set, constantly emitting radiance; and the color of his lips is a beautiful red, like the *bimba* fruit.'"

At that time, King Wonderful Adornment, having praised the Buddha for such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of merits, joined his palms with single-minded devotion before the Tathāgata and addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One!
It is truly unprecedented! The Dharma of the Tathāgata is fully perfected, possessing inconceivable and subtle merits; its teachings, precepts, and practices are peaceful, secure, and wholesome.
"From this day forward, I shall no longer act according to my own whims; I shall not give rise to false views, arrogance, anger, or any other evil thoughts.
Having spoken these words, he prostrated before the Buddha and departed.
The Buddha addressed the great assembly: "What do you think?
Who else could King Wondrous Adornment have been?"
The Bodhisattva Flower Virtue (Huade) is that very person.

As for Lady Pure Virtue (Jingde), she is the Bodhisattva Radiant Adorned Appearance (Guangzao Zhuangyanxiang) now before the Buddha; out of compassion for King Wondrous Adornment and his retinue, she was born there.
Those two sons are now the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja and the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata.

These Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata have accomplished such great merits as these; they have planted the roots of all virtues under immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, and have accomplished inconceivable wholesome merits.
"If there are those who know the names of these two bodhisattvas, all the devas and people of the world should also pay them homage.
When the Buddha preached this "Chapter on the Past Deeds of King Subhavyūha," eighty-four thousand people became free from dust and defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena.

Chapter Twenty-Six: The Encouragement of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, endowed with sovereign supernormal powers, majestic virtue, and renown, arrived from the east accompanied by an immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable number of great bodhisattvas. As they passed through various lands, all those regions trembled; precious lotus flowers rained down, and hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of diverse kinds of musical instruments played in concert.

Furthermore, surrounded by a great assembly of countless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, each manifesting their majestic power and supernatural abilities, they arrived at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa in the Sahā world. They prostrated themselves with their heads at the feet of Śākyamuni Buddha, circumambulated him seven times to the right, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

From the land of the Buddha Ratnatejobhyudgatarāja, I have heard from afar that the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* is being preached in this Sahā world; therefore, together with immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of bodhisattvas, I have come to hear and receive it.
We only pray that the World-Honored One will explain this for us: how can sons and daughters of good family, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, obtain this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*?
The Buddha told Samantabhadra Bodhisattva:
"If good sons or good daughters accomplish four dharmas, they shall obtain this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata:

first, being protected and remembered by all Buddhas; second, planting the roots of all virtues; third, entering the stage of right determination (*samyaktvaniyāma*); and fourth, giving rise to the mind that seeks to save all sentient beings."
“Good sons and good daughters, by accomplishing these four dharmas in this way, they will certainly obtain this sutra after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

In the final five hundred years, during this age of turbidity and evil, for those who receive, uphold, and recite this sutra, I shall provide protection, eliminate their misfortunes and afflictions, and cause them to attain peace and security. I shall ensure that no one seeking to find an opportunity against them can succeed—neither Māras, nor Māra’s sons, nor Māra’s daughters, nor Māra’s subjects; neither those possessed by Māra, nor yakṣas, nor rākṣasas, nor kumbhāṇḍas, nor piśācas, nor kiṃkaras, nor pūtanas, nor vetālas, nor any other beings who torment humans. None of these shall be able to gain the upper hand.

If this person, whether walking or standing, recites this sutra, at that time I shall mount the six-tusked white elephant king and, together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas, go to their location and manifest my own form before them. I shall provide offerings, protect them, and comfort their minds, all for the sake of making offerings to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
If this person sits and contemplates this sutra, at that time I shall again mount the king of white elephants and manifest before that person.
If that person has forgotten or lost even a single word or a single verse of this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, I shall instruct them and recite it with them, restoring their mastery of the text.

At that time, those who receive, uphold, read, and recite the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* shall behold my body; they will experience great joy and become even more diligent. Because they have seen me, they will immediately attain samādhis and dhāraṇīs, namely: the Dhāraṇī of Revolving, the Dhāraṇī of Hundreds of Thousands of Myriads of Billions of Revolutions, and the Dhāraṇī of Skillful Means in the Sound of the Dharma. They shall attain such dhāraṇīs as these.
“World-Honored One!

If, in a future age, during the final five hundred years of the turbid and evil world, there should be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who seek, uphold, recite, copy, or desire to practice this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, they should for twenty-one days practice with single-minded diligence. When those twenty-one days are complete, I shall mount a six-tusked white elephant and, surrounded by immeasurable bodhisattvas, manifest before that person a body that all sentient beings delight to behold, and preach the Dharma for them, instructing, benefiting, and gladdening them.”

I shall also bestow upon them this dhāraṇī mantra; because they have obtained this dhāraṇī, no non-human being shall be able to destroy them, nor shall they be deluded or disturbed by women, and I myself shall also constantly protect such persons.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will listen as I recite this dhāraṇī.
Thereupon, before the Buddha, he spoke the mantra, saying:
Tadyathā | atanda-atanda-pati |
Daṇḍa-vrata-ni-daṇḍa-kuśa-śīghra-kṛ-daṇḍa-sudhāri.
Sūtra sūtra vati buddha bhasmani dhāraṇi aparājitā rātrī saṃgha pālī kīrte.
Saṃghāṅgātānīdarāmbārīkīkaravāsata-vahurda-kaucchara-ānugātiṅgi-bi-kiri-tiṅgi. “World-Honored One! [Thus it was said.]”

If there are bodhisattvas who hear this dhāraṇī, they should know it is through the supernatural power of Samantabhadra. If there are those who receive and uphold the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* as it circulates throughout Jambudvīpa, they should think:
"All of this is due to the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra."

"If there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, correctly contemplate, and understand the meaning and intent [of this teaching], and practice according to what is taught, you should know that these persons perform the conduct of Samantabhadra; they have deeply planted roots of goodness in the presence of immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, and all Tathāgatas will stroke their heads with their hands."

If one merely copies [this sutra], at the end of that person's life, they shall be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; at that time, eighty-four thousand celestial maidens will come to welcome them with various musical performances, and the person will immediately don a crown of the seven treasures and enjoy themselves in pleasure among the court ladies.
How much more so for those who receive, uphold, read, recite, correctly contemplate, understand its meaning and intent, and practice according to the teaching!

If there is anyone who receives, upholds, reads, recites, and understands its meaning and intent, at the end of that person's life, a thousand Buddhas will extend their hands to them, ensuring they are not terrified and do not fall into the evil realms, but shall immediately go to the presence of Maitreya Bodhisattva in the Tuṣita Heaven above.

The Bodhisattva Maitreya, endowed with the thirty-two marks and surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattvas, was born therein amidst hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of celestial maidens as his retinue.

Since there are such merits and benefits as these, the wise person should single-mindedly write it themselves, or have others write it, and then receive, uphold, read, recite, correctly contemplate, and practice according to its teachings.
World-Honored One!
By my supernatural powers, I shall now protect this sutra, so that after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, it may be widely circulated within Jambudvīpa and never be interrupted.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent! Samantabhadra!”

That you are able to protect and assist this sutra, bringing peace, happiness, and benefit to many sentient beings, shows that you have already accomplished inconceivable merit and profound, great compassion. Having long ago resolved your mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, you are able to make such a vow of supernatural power to protect this sutra; I, too, shall use my own supernatural powers to protect those who are able to receive and uphold the name of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
“Samantabhadra!

If there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, correctly contemplate, cultivate, or transcribe this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, you should know that such persons see Śākyamuni Buddha; it should be known that such persons hear this sūtra directly from the Buddha’s own mouth;
and it should be known that such persons make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha.”
One should know that such a person is praised by the Buddha with the words, "Excellent!";
one should know that such a person has had his head stroked by the hand of Śākyamuni Buddha;
one should know that such a person is covered by the robe of Śākyamuni Buddha.

Such a person no longer craves worldly pleasures, nor do they take delight in the scriptures or writings of non-Buddhist paths, nor do they enjoy associating with such people or with evildoers—whether butchers, those who raise pigs, sheep, chickens, or dogs, hunters, or those who trade in female beauty. This person’s mind is upright and honest; they possess right mindfulness and the power of merit.
They are not afflicted by the three poisons, nor are they troubled by envy, pride, false pride, or overweening pride.
Having few desires and being content, this person is able to cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra.
“Samantabhadra!

If, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, during the final five hundred years, there should be anyone who sees another receiving, upholding, reading, or reciting the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, you should form this thought:

‘This person shall before long proceed to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) and destroy the hosts of Māras; they shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, turn the wheel of Dharma, beat the drum of Dharma, blow the conch of Dharma, and rain down the rain of Dharma; they shall sit upon the lion throne of Dharma amidst the great assembly of devas and humans.’”

“Samantabhadra! If, in a future age, there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, such persons shall no longer be greedily attached to clothing, bedding, food and drink, or articles for daily life; their aspirations shall not be in vain, and they shall likewise obtain their karmic rewards in this present life.”
If someone disparages them, saying: "You are merely a madman;
practicing such deeds in vain, you will ultimately gain nothing," they shall suffer this retribution of sin by being blind life after life.
If there are those who make offerings to or praise [this teaching], they shall obtain visible retribution in this very life.
Furthermore, if one sees someone who upholds this sutra and exposes their faults or evils, [one incurs grave consequences].

Whether the statement be true or false, such a person shall suffer from leprosy in this present life; furthermore, those who mock them with derision shall, in every successive birth, have teeth that are sparse and missing, ugly lips, flat noses, and contorted hands and feet; their eyes shall be squinted, their bodies foul-smelling and filthy, and they shall suffer from malignant sores, pus, blood, dropsy, shortness of breath, and various other grave and evil diseases.
"Therefore, Samantabhadra!
If you see one who receives and upholds this sutra, you should go out to meet them from afar and pay them respect as you would the Buddha.

When this "Chapter on Samantabhadra’s Exhortation" was spoken, bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, immeasurable and boundless, attained hundreds of thousands of billions of *dhāraṇīs* of revolution; and bodhisattvas equal in number to the atoms within a trichiliocosm became fully endowed with the path of Samantabhadra.

Chapter Twenty-Seven: Entrustment The Added Chapter on the Entrustment of the Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma, Chapter Twenty-Seven. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha rose from his seat and manifested great supernormal powers. With his right hand, he stroked the heads of immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and spoke these words:

"For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, I have cultivated and accumulated this rare Dharma of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. I now entrust it to you; you should with one mind disseminate this Dharma, causing it to increase and spread far and wide."
Thus, he placed his hand upon the crowns of the heads of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and spoke these words:

"For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, I have cultivated and gathered this Dharma of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, which is so difficult to attain. I now entrust it to you; you should receive, uphold, read, recite, and widely proclaim this Dharma, so that all sentient beings may universally hear and know it."

Why is this? Because the Tathāgata possesses great compassion, is free from all stinginess and parsimony, and is without fear; he is able to bestow upon sentient beings the wisdom of a Buddha, the wisdom of a Tathāgata, and self-arisen wisdom.

The Tathāgata is the great donor to all sentient beings; you, too, should follow and learn the Dharma of the Tathāgata, and do not give rise to stinginess. In future ages, if there are good men or good women who have faith in the wisdom of the Tathāgata, you should expound this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* for them so that they may hear and know it, in order to enable those people to attain the Buddha-wisdom.
If there are sentient beings who do not believe or accept [this], you should instruct, benefit, and gladden them by pointing them toward other profound dharmas of the Tathāgata.
If you are able to act in this way, you will have repaid the kindness of all the Buddhas.

When the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas heard the Buddha speak these words, great joy filled their entire bodies; they increased their reverence all the more, bowing with bent bodies and lowered heads, and joining their palms toward the Buddha, they spoke in unison:
"As the World-Honored One has commanded, we shall fully carry it out."
"So be it, World-Honored One!
We pray that you have no concern.
Thus did the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas speak in unison three times.
“As the World-Honored One has commanded, we shall carry it out fully.
So be it, World-Honored One!
We pray that you have no further concern.”
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha commanded the various emanation Buddhas who had come from the ten directions to each return to their own lands, saying:
"May the Buddhas each abide as they please; the stupa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha may now return to its former state."

When these words were spoken, the immeasurable Buddhas from the ten directions who were seated upon lion thrones beneath jeweled trees, as well as the Buddha Prabhūtaratna, the boundless assembly of asaṃkhyeya bodhisattvas such as Urdhvaja, the fourfold assembly of śrāvakas headed by Śāriputra, and all the world’s devas, humans, and asuras, hearing what the Buddha had said, were all filled with great joy.
